newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Jardine Fleming survey finds HK investors bullish.
newsitem.headline: Jardine Fleming survey finds HK investors bullish.

text.p: A survey of local Hong Kong investors found that most are positive on the outlook for the Hang Seng index, Jardine Fleming Unit Trusts said on Monday.

In a telephone survey of 200 Hong Kong-based investors taken between June 10 and 16, 55 percent of those questioned considered it likely that they would invest in the local stock market, either directly or through trusts, within the next six months.
The figure was marginally down from the previous survey, taken in February.
Nearly 40 percent of those surveyed in June think the market will be above 15,000 in six months' time, compared with only 15 percent previously.
Only 14 percent think the market will be lower in six months time.
Half of respondents also said they expect the Hang Seng index to be higher in a year's time. The proportion expecting the index to be above 15,000 was 45 percent, compared with 25 percent previously.

The survey, which was conducted by Market Behaviour (HK) for Jardine Fleming and the Hong Kong Economic Times, surveyed 200 adults in Hong Kong. All had existing investments in unit trusts, stocks, foreign currency savings accounts or bank term deposits.
The Hang Seng Index closed on Monday at 15,021, down 133 points, or 0.88 percent.
